variables.label: Cabin CO2

source.label: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 [V2 6004]: 1-hour average ppCO2 at or below 3 mmHg (about 3947 ppm), OCHMO-TB-004

variables.note: The standard limits the 1-hour average; the simulation compares each 15-minute sample, which gives the same answer for episodes longer than an hour.

variables.label: Cabin temperature

source.label: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 [V2 6012] crew health limit 18-27 °C and [V2 6013] crew performance zone 20-25 °C, OCHMO-TB-002 (ECLSS)

variables.note: The standard defines the limits as a joint temperature and humidity envelope; this prototype checks each variable against its own range.

variables.label: Relative humidity

source.label: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 [V2 6012] crew health limit 25-75 % and [V2 6013] crew performance zone 30-60 %, OCHMO-TB-002 (ECLSS)

variables.note: Same joint envelope caveat as cabin temperature.

variables.label: Radiation dose (mission total)

source.label: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev C [V1 4030]: career effective dose below 600 mSv

variables.note: Context only. No NASA source in this repository links ISS-level dose rates to an acute change in heart rate, blood pressure or the other monitored vitals, so dose never explains an atypical reading. The career limit counts all flights; the running total shown covers this mission only. The simulated dose rate is illustrative and not taken from a NASA source.

links.effect: Elevated CO2 is listed among the environmental conditions that reduce sleep quality and quantity; the CO2 brief lists decreased sleep at high exposure.

source.label: OCHMO sleep accommodations technical brief (NASA-STD-3001): elevated CO2, noise, temperature and humidity affect sleep

links.effect: ISS crew cite temperature among the reasons for reduced sleep on orbit; a cold cabin was one reason Apollo 11 crew could not sleep.

source.label: OCHMO sleep accommodations technical brief (NASA-STD-3001): reasons cited by ISS crew for reduced sleep

links.effect: Humidity is listed among the environmental conditions that affect sleep quality and quantity.

source.label: OCHMO sleep accommodations technical brief (NASA-STD-3001): environmental conditions that affect sleep

links.effect: Heat strain models predict heart rate from the ambient environment (with work, clothing and acclimation); a warm cabin is expected to raise heart rate.

source.label: Pandolf et al., heat strain prediction of rectal temperature, heart rate and sweat loss from the environment, NASA SOAR 1993 (NTRS 19940029146)

links.effect: Heat strain models predict core (rectal) temperature from the ambient environment; a warm cabin is expected to raise body temperature.

source.label: Pandolf et al., heat strain prediction of rectal temperature, heart rate and sweat loss from the environment, NASA SOAR 1993 (NTRS 19940029146)
